title: Tool orchestration: result injection, chaining policies, and recursion guards
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: The Core API currently supports single-step tool/function calls and streaming responses, but lacks a robust, secure execution loop for orchestrating multiple tool invocations in one request. Customers building agents and tool chains require predictable chaining behavior, safe result injection into model context, and guardrails to prevent runaway recursion or amplifier loops.

Goal: Design and implement a tool execution loop that supports: multi-tool chaining with explicit policies (sequential, parallel-with-merge), deterministic result injection envelopes (metadata + provenance), streaming partial structured outputs to clients as tools complete, and runtime guards (max_steps, depth, cycle-detection, idempotency tokens). Ensure backward compatibility via a compatibility layer for older SDKs and maintainable observability for debugging and audits.

Scope:
- API: extend the existing /v1/generate/chat endpoint with a tool_execution block that can express a chain plan and runtime guards.
- Runtime: implement scheduler that can execute tool calls, merge results (configurable merge strategies), inject sanitized outputs into the LLM context, and stream incremental structured events to the client.
- Safety & limits: max_tool_invocations per request, recursion depth limit, per-tool timeouts, dedup detection for tool loops, and explicit opt-in for tools that modify external state.
- Compatibility: add a translation layer so legacy clients that send single-tool calls get a default tool_execution plan and can opt-in to new behaviors gradually.
- Telemetry: emit traceable events including tool_run_id, parent_request_id, tool_inputs_hash, and guard-triggered reasons to the Console and logs.

Non-goals: designing new tool SDKs or adding new tool types (webhooks, adapters) beyond current function calling and the existing tools surface. This ticket focuses on orchestration and safety primitives.
acceptance_criteria: API accepts a tool_execution plan specifying an ordered list of tools and guard parameters and returns 202 with a streaming event envelope when execution begins

Runtime executes multiple tool calls according to the plan, merges results according to configured strategies (append, overwrite, structured-merge), and injects the merged content into the model context without leaking raw creds or secrets
Recursion/loop guard rules prevent more than configured max_steps and detect repetitive invocation cycles (same tool sequence repeated) to abort with a structured error and code TOOL_LOOP_DETECTED
Clients can receive partial structured output events (tool_started, tool_result, merge_applied, model_progress, tool_error) in the same streaming session
Compatibility layer converts legacy single-call requests into a one-step tool_execution plan and preserves existing response shapes unless client opts into structured streaming
Integration test harness simulates agent-style multi-tool conversations and checks that provenance metadata (tool_run_id, tool_version, execution_index) is present for every injected result
Canary rollout in dedicated-env with telemetry flag shows no >0.1% increase in latency P95 for non-tool traffic and stable error rates
design_decisions: Use a strict result envelope for each tool: {tool_run_id, tool_name, tool_version, status, payload, sanitized:true/false, start_ts, end_ts}. The payload will be stringified structured JSON; runtime will perform schema validation before injection.
Default merge strategy is 'append' for untyped outputs and 'structured-merge' for outputs that declare a schema. Allow per-plan override.

Implement loop guards with two orthogonal checks: (1) max_steps (global per-request limit, default 10), (2) cycle-detection using a rolling hash of (tool_name + input_hash) sequence — if a sequence repeats beyond threshold, abort.

Inject results into model context as ephemeral system messages that include provenance headers; do not include raw or secret fields (runtime sanitizer will drop keys matching regexes configured per-tool).
Expose explicit idempotency tokens on tool calls so retries can be collapsed server-side to avoid duplicate side-effects.
Compatibility layer will run in the API gateway and add a tool_execution wrapper for legacy clients; SDKs will be updated to surface opt-in flags over next two releases.

Streaming event schema will be stable and backwards compatible: each line is a JSON envelope with event_type and event_payload. Older clients will receive final_text as before when not subscribed to streaming structured events.
implementation_plan: API: add tool_execution schema + validation (gateway) — PR# github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls/1832
Runtime: scheduler + executor changes, implement result envelopes and sanitizer — PR# github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pulls/907
SDK: add opt-in streaming structured client and helper to build tool_execution plan — PR# github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pulls/451
Telemetry: add new trace fields and Console dashboard for tool run metrics — dashboard link: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/tool-exec-overview
Tests: unit tests for sanitizer, merge strategies; end-to-end tests in CI simulating 1k agent-style conversations
Canary: rollout to dedicated-env cluster with feature flag 'tool_exec_v2' for 10% traffic, monitor latency and errors for 48h
Docs: write API spec and migration guide and example agent recipes (Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/Tool+Execution+Loop)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Tool results accidentally leak secrets into the prompt. Mitigation: runtime sanitizer with denylist patterns + per-tool optical scanning and post-injection assertion tests.
Risk: Long-running tool chains increase tail latency. Mitigation: enforce per-tool timeouts, global max_steps, optional async 'deferred' execution mode returning a job id.
Risk: Backwards compatibility break for older SDKs. Mitigation: compatibility translation layer in gateway and staged SDK releases with opt-in flags.
Risk: Increased operational cost from higher telemetry volume. Mitigation: sample tool events at 1% by default and provide customer-level opt-in for full traces.
Risk: Agent loops create stateful side-effects (duplicate writes). Mitigation: require explicit 'side_effects_allowed' flag on plan and enforce idempotency tokens for tools that mutate state.
